messages:
sara: Heads up — saw a spike of 429s from Tempo during yesterday's canary (svc-payments). P95 ingest latency jumped and a bunch of spans got dropped. Anyone else see this?

matt: Yup, saw it too. Tempo ingesters returned 429s once the write QPS spiked. Our OTLP exporter retries, but the bursts still cause downstream pressure.

oleg: Also noticed some trace IDs are landing on multiple ingesters after the rollout — seems like the shard key change didn't finish reconciling. Could be amplifying the 429s.

jess: Is the fallback flow to honeycomb enabled? We have a secondary exporter but it's only used for debug traces right now. Might be worth routing high-verbosity or sampled=1 traces there temporarily. :thinking_face:

karen: Proposal idea: add a short-term routing rule that (a) smooths retries with a retry-budget, (b) token-buckets per-tenant to limit spikes, and (c) routes overflow to fallback exporters. Pseudo config: 
```yaml
exporters:
  tempo:
    endpoints: ["tempo-east:4317"]
    retry_policy:
      budget: 0.1    # fraction of requests allowed to retry
      min_backoff_ms: 100
  honeycomb:
    api_key: REDACTED
routing:
  - match: "resource.service.name == 'payments' and attributes['env'] == 'canary'"
    action:
      - send_to: [tempo]
      - overflow_to: [honeycomb, jaeger]
      - apply_rate_limit: 2000  # spans/sec per-tenant
```

matt: That looks reasonable. Two questions: how do we detect "overflow" reliably? We have ingest-utilization metrics, but they're a bit delayed. Maybe use a rolling log of 429 rate > 0.5% over 30s as a trigger.

oleg: For the shard mismatch, we should avoid rehashing live traffic. Plan: drain one ingester ring at a time, run the reconciliation job to move ranges, then un-drain. I'll sketch a runbook.

jess: If we route to honeycomb/jaeger as overflow, we need to map span IDs/trace IDs consistently so the console can reconstruct traces. Any exporter transformations? We currently have a small mapping shim for Honeycomb. Make sure it preserves trace_id and parent_id.

karen: Also consider retention tiers — if we overflow to honeycomb, we probably want a lower retention TTL for those overflowed traces (e.g., 7d) vs normal 30d in Tempo to control cost. This should be part of the routing rule metadata.

infra-bot: alert: tempo-ingester-429 rate=0.74% window=5m triggered at 2026-11-12T17:22:10Z

matt: Good catch. Action items: (1) karen to draft routing rule + retry-budget PR, (2) oleg to write reconcile runbook and coordinate a one-ingester drain test, (3) jess to verify honeycomb mapping preserves IDs and TTL override, (4) sara to add a temporary dashboard tile showing tempo-ingest-429, per-tenant QPS, and fallback-rate.

sara: I'll add the dashboard and a per-tenant heatmap; will also add a quick playbook note for oncall to flip the routing rule if 429s > 0.5% for 5m.

oleg: One extra gotcha — if we do token-bucket per-tenant we must gate it behind a config flag so Dedicated customers can opt out. Put the default to opt-in in prod for now.

jess: I'll run a small canary by routing 5% of payments traces to honeycomb with the mapping preserved and TTL=7d, then monitor error/latency.

matt: If anyone wants to pair on the retry-budget algorithm, ping me. We should pick sensible defaults to avoid double-retries and thundering herd.

karen: I'll open the PR for the exporter routing policy + TTL metadata tonight.

sara: Thanks all — let's sync tomorrow after the reconcile dry-run. :thumbsup:
